purpose: Organize broad home, mortgage, association and land-use questions before using an official source or choosing a qualified Tennessee professional.
boundary: General information and document organization only—not legal advice, a deadline calculation, code interpretation, a title opinion, foreclosure prevention, representation or a prediction.
todayBoundary: For immediate danger call 911. For a posted notice, threatened lockout, sale date, court paper or deadline that may require action today, contact the named Tennessee court, agency, servicer or a qualified attorney now.

documentRoles.label: Mortgage, lease, deed or association document
Official property, permit or court record
Payment or account record kept privately

tracks.title: Mortgage, foreclosure or sale-notice preparation
steps: Record the exact document title, sender and every printed date without uploading it.
Separate what the notice states from what you still need to verify.
Confirm the servicer, court or sale information through an official route.
Prepare questions about review options, timing, fees and representation.
Keep originals and account details private and seek qualified Tennessee help promptly.
questions: Which printed date may control and how can I verify it?
Which Tennessee process or court applies?
What review, response or assistance routes should I ask about?

tracks.title: HOA, condominium or association-notice preparation
steps: Identify the association document and action requested.
Record cited provisions and printed dates exactly without interpreting them.
List governing documents and communications you have privately.
Separate correction, hearing, appeal, payment and legal-review questions.
Verify association procedures and Tennessee rights with a responsible source.
questions: Which governing provision is being cited?
What internal review or hearing path is stated?
Which Tennessee professional can review the documents and dates?

tracks.title: Zoning, land-use or development-notice preparation
steps: Confirm whether the property is within Franklin or another jurisdiction.
Record the application, parcel, meeting or notice identifiers.
Use the responsible official planning or zoning source for the current record.
Prepare questions about participation dates, required formats and the public record.
Separate factual comments from legal or engineering conclusions.
questions: Which authority and process apply to this parcel?
Where is the official current record?
How and when may the public participate?

tracks.title: Home document review preparation
steps: Choose only broad document roles—do not paste or upload document text.
Mark which document has a printed date, named party, requested action or reference number.
Compare the same broad fields across selected documents.
List conflicts and missing items as questions, not conclusions.
Carry the originals to an official source or qualified professional for interpretation.
questions: Do the documents name the same parties and property?
Which dates or requested actions differ?
Which document controls and who can verify that?
